verses.zh: 「你们不要论断人，免得你们被论断。
verses.en: “Do not judge so that you will not be judged.[NOTE:1]
notes: The point of the statement do not judge so that you will not be judged is that the standards we apply to others God applies to us. The passive verb will not be judged has God is the unstated performer of the action. Such usage is generally thought to have arisen within Judaism out of the tendency to minimize the mention of God’s name out of reverence for God, and carried over into early Christian tradition, although in this particular verse the agent may be left unstated more for rhetorical effect. See also ExSyn 437-38.

verses.zh: 因为你们怎样论断人，也必怎样被论断；你们用甚么量器量给人，也必用甚么量器量给你们。
verses.en: For by the standard you judge you will be judged, and the measure you use will be the measure you receive.[NOTE:1]
notes: The term translated speck (KJV, ASV “mote”; NAB “splinter”) refers to a small piece of wood, chaff, or straw; see L&N 3.66.

verses.zh: 为甚么看见你弟兄眼中有刺，却不想自己眼中有梁木呢？
verses.en: Why[NOTE:1] do you see the speck[NOTE:2] in your brother’s eye, but fail to see[NOTE:3] the beam of wood[NOTE:4] in your own?
notes: Or “do not notice.”
The term beam of wood refers to a very big piece of wood, the main beam of a building, in contrast to the speck in the other’s eye (L&N 7.78).

Or “otherwise the latter will trample them under their feet and the former will turn around and tear you to pieces.” This verse is sometimes understood as a chiasm of the pattern a-b-b-a, in which the first and last clauses belong together (“dogs…turn around and tear you to pieces”) and the second and third clauses belong together (“pigs…trample them under their feet”).

Many interpreters see the three present imperatives (Ask…seek…knock) as mainly limited to persistence in prayer (cf. v. 11), though others see them referring more generally to taking the initiative with God in various ways.tn The three present imperatives in this verse are best viewed as iterative (Wallace, ExSyn 722, lists the verse as an example of this usage), calling for repeated action.

verses.zh: 你自己眼中有梁木，怎能对你弟兄说：『容我去掉你眼中的刺』呢？
verses.en: Or how can you say[NOTE:1] to your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye,’ while there is a beam in your own?
notes: Grk “it”; the referent (a door) is implied by the context and has been specified in the translation here and in v. 8 for clarity.

verses.zh: 你这假冒为善的人！先去掉自己眼中的梁木，然后才能看得清楚，去掉你弟兄眼中的刺。
verses.en: You hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

verses.zh: 不要把圣物给狗，也不要把你们的珍珠丢在猪前，恐怕它践踏了珍珠，转过来咬你们。」
verses.en: Do not give what is holy to dogs or throw your pearls before pigs; otherwise they will trample them under their feet and turn around and tear you to pieces.[NOTE:1]
notes: The actions of asking, seeking, and knocking are repeated here from v. 7 with the additional encouragement that God does respond to such requests/actions.

verses.zh: 「你们祈求，就给你们；寻找，就寻见；叩门，就给你们开门。
verses.en: “Ask[NOTE:1] and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door[NOTE:2] will be opened for you.
notes: Grk “Or is there.”
The two questions of vv. 9-10 use a construction in Greek that expects a negative answer: “No parent would do this!”

verses.zh: 因为凡祈求的，就得着；寻找的，就寻见；叩门的，就给他开门。
verses.en: For everyone who asks[NOTE:1] receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
notes: The participle ὄντες (ontes) has been translated as a concessive adverbial participle: in spite of the fact that the hearers are “evil,” they still know how to give “good gifts” to their own children (see also ExSyn 634).

verses.zh: 你们中间谁有儿子求饼，反给他石头呢？
verses.en: Is[NOTE:1] there anyone among you who, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?
notes: The provision of the good gifts is probably a reference to the wisdom and guidance supplied in response to repeated requests. The teaching as a whole stresses not that we get everything we want, but that God gives the good that we need.

verses.zh: 求鱼，反给他蛇呢？
verses.en: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “Therefore in.” Here οὖν (oun) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 你们虽然不好，尚且知道拿好东西给儿女，何况你们在天上的父，岂不更把好东西给求他的人吗？
verses.en: If you then, although you are evil,[NOTE:1] know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good gifts[NOTE:2] to those who ask him!
notes: Jesus’ teaching as reflected in the phrase treat others as you would want them to treat you, known generally as the Golden Rule, is not completely unique in the ancient world, but here it is stated in its most emphatic, selfless form. It is stated negatively in Tobit 4:15, and can also be found in the Talmud in a story about the great rabbi Hillel, who is said to have told a Gentile who asked to be taught the Torah, “What is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbor; that is the whole Torah, while the rest is the commentary thereof; go and learn it” (b. Shabbat 31a).
Grk “is”; cf. CEV “This is what the Law and the Prophets are all about”; NIV “for this sums up the Law and the Prophets.”

verses.zh: 所以，无论何事，你们愿意人怎样待你们，你们也要怎样待人，因为这就是律法和先知的道理。」
verses.en: In[NOTE:1] everything, treat others as you would want them[NOTE:2] to treat you,[NOTE:3] for this fulfills[NOTE:4] the law and the prophets.
notes: The same verb is used in Matt 5:20, suggesting that the kingdom of heaven is to be understood here as the object.
See BDAG 1007 s.v. τίς for the translation of τί (ti) as an exclamation.

Here the destination is specified as life. In several places Matthew uses “life” or “eternal life” in proximity with “the kingdom of heaven,” suggesting a close relationship between the two concepts (compare Matt 25:34 with v. 46; Matt 19:16, 17, 29 with vv. 23, 24). Matthew consistently portrays “eternal life” as something a person enters in the world to come, whereas the Gospel of John sees “eternal life” as beginning in the present and continuing into the future (cf. John 5:24).

The identity of these false prophets is not specified, and this has led to a wide variety of suggested referents: the Pharisees, the Zealots, the Essenes (all roughly contemporaries of Jesus), later groups (representatives of Pauline Christianity, the Gnostics) or later individuals (Simon Magus mentioned in Acts 8:9-24, Bar Kokhba who led the Jewish revolt of A.D. 132-35), or the eschatological false prophets who will lead people astray in the end times (Matt 24:24). Of course, some of these suggestions assume a second century date for the composition (or redaction) of the Gospel of Matthew.

verses.zh: 「你们要进窄门。因为引到灭亡，那门是宽的，路是大的，进去的人也多；
verses.en: “Enter[NOTE:1] through the narrow gate because the gate is wide and the way is spacious that leads to destruction, and there are many who enter through it.
notes: Sheep’s clothing…voracious wolves. Jesus uses a metaphor here to point out that these false prophets appear to be one thing, but in reality they are something quite different and dangerous.

verses.zh: 引到永生，那门是窄的，路是小的，找着的人也少。」
verses.en: How[NOTE:1] narrow is the gate and difficult the way that leads to life,[NOTE:2] and there are few who find it!
notes: Grk “They do not gather.” This has been simplified to the passive voice in the translation since the subject “they” is not specified further in the context.

The statement illustrates the principle: That which cannot produce fruit does not produce fruit.tn The Greek construction anticipates a negative answer. This is indicated in the translation by the ‘tag’ question “are they?” at the end of the sentence.

verses.zh: 「你们要防备假先知。他们到你们这里来，外面披着羊皮，里面却是残暴的狼。
verses.en: “Watch out for false prophets,[NOTE:1] who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are voracious wolves.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “rotten.” The word σαπρός, modifying “tree” in both v. 17 and 18, can also mean “diseased” (L&N 65.28).
The double use of the vocative is normally used in situations of high emotion or emphasis. Even an emphatic confession like this one without corresponding action means little.

verses.zh: 凭着他们的果子，就可以认出他们来。荆棘上岂能摘葡萄呢？蒺藜里岂能摘无花果呢？
verses.en: You will recognize them by their fruit. Grapes are not gathered[NOTE:1] from thorns or figs from thistles, are they?[NOTE:2]
notes: The phrase “in your name” occurs before each of the verbs in the Greek text, making it somewhat emphatic, but the phrase was placed after the verbs in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Or “you who commit lawless deeds”; or “you who behave lawlessly”; Grk “workers of lawlessness.”

verses.zh: 这样，凡好树都结好果子，惟独坏树结坏果子。
verses.en: In the same way, every good tree bears good fruit, but the bad[NOTE:1] tree bears bad fruit.
notes: Grk “Therefore everyone.” Here οὖν (oun) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 好树不能结坏果子；坏树不能结好果子。
verses.en: A good tree is not able to bear bad fruit, nor a bad tree to bear good fruit.

verses.zh: 凡不结好果子的树就砍下来，丢在火里。
verses.en: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

verses.zh: 所以，凭着他们的果子就可以认出他们来。」
verses.en: So then, you will recognize them by their fruit.

verses.zh: 「凡称呼我『主啊，主啊』的人不能都进天国；惟独遵行我天父旨意的人才能进去。
verses.en: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’[NOTE:1] will enter into the kingdom of heaven—only the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.
notes: Grk “will be like.” The same phrase occurs in v. 26.

verses.zh: 当那日必有许多人对我说：『主啊，主啊，我们不是奉你的名传道，奉你的名赶鬼，奉你的名行许多异能吗？』
verses.en: On that day, many will say to me, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many powerful deeds in your name?’[NOTE:1]
notes: Here and in v. 26 the Greek text reads ἀνήρ (anēr), while the parallel account in Luke 6:47-49 uses ἄνθρωπος (anthrōpos) in vv. 48 and 49.

verses.zh: 我就明明地告诉他们说：『我从来不认识你们，你们这些作恶的人，离开我去吧！』」
verses.en: Then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you. Go away from me, you lawbreakers!’[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “the rivers.”

verses.zh: 「所以，凡听见我这话就去行的，好比一个聪明人，把房子盖在磐石上；
verses.en: “Everyone[NOTE:1] who hears these words of mine and does them is like[NOTE:2] a wise man[NOTE:3] who built his house on rock.
notes: Jesus’ teaching impressed the hearers with the directness of its claim; he taught with authority. A study of Jewish rabbinic interpretation shows that it was typical to cite a list of authorities to make one’s point. Jesus addressed the issues directly, in terms of his own understanding, without citing other teachers.
Or “their scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 2:4.

verses.zh: 雨淋，水冲，风吹，撞着那房子，房子总不倒塌，因为根基立在磐石上。
verses.en: The rain fell, the flood[NOTE:1] came, and the winds beat against that house, but it did not collapse because its foundation had been laid on rock.

verses.zh: 凡听见我这话不去行的，好比一个无知的人，把房子盖在沙土上；
verses.en: Everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.

verses.zh: 雨淋，水冲，风吹，撞着那房子，房子就倒塌了，并且倒塌得很大。」
verses.en: The rain fell, the flood came, and the winds beat against that house, and it collapsed—it was utterly destroyed!”[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 耶稣讲完了这些话，众人都希奇他的教训；
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] Jesus finished saying these things, the crowds were amazed by his teaching,

verses.zh: 因为他教训他们，正像有权柄的人，不像他们的文士。
verses.en: because he taught them like one who had authority,[NOTE:1] not like their experts in the law.[NOTE:2]
